analysis:
The supplied units are documentation only: docs/architecture/inference.md (head excerpts at lines 1235-1808, plus changed ranges at 619-625, 869-905 and 1767) and docs/developer/serving-performance-qualification.md (date bump and a paragraph on admission-estimator corrections). No source code, key handling, attestation, encryption, authorization, or wire-protocol behavior changes in the supplied evidence.

The documented changes concern (a) freshness anchoring for EnginePerformanceMeasurements.Rate with out-of-order observations, and (b) three TTFT admission estimator corrections (per-batch-step decode charging via CBv2DecodeRateShape) gated by DARKBLOOM_TTFT_ADMISSION_FIXES=0 as a rollback. These affect scheduling and admission availability (relevant to T-010, T-029 and DoS-style concerns). They do not touch the prefix-cache storage posture in T-041: TTL, disk budget, HMAC naming and AAD are unchanged. The docs retain statements that the SSD checkpoint identity is unchanged and that qualification is separate from the automatic intent.

The existing prose in the head text states that the sampler is not part of prompt or cache identity, that MiMo/Qwen4/Bonsai paths are unqualified candidates, and that no catalog or release is activated. I found no claim that weakens the threat model, and no new trust-boundary language.

Remaining questions for integration: the estimator and freshness-anchoring code paths (AdmissionRateEstimators.swift, EnginePerformanceMeasurements) are not in this batch. The truncated patch excerpt for inference.md (lines 869-905) was not fully visible, so the doc claims about the scaling bound could not be checked against the code. Any admission-underestimate risk from the estimator change would be a code-level concern outside this documentation-only unit.
